chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Summer at Ben Allen's place with the two Ethels
summary: He works a season at Kentucky and Arctic Avenue with Ethel Waters, Ethel Williams, Snow Fisher and Izzy Ringgold, and says Waters was an entertainer not a great singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, where did you then, when you got back to Atlantic City, where did you perform?
Well, when I come back to Atlantic City I was getting a band together and a man named Ben Allen had a

place at Kentucky and Arctic Avenue. And then he was just turning his place over to another MAN called Charley, um, anyhow this fellow was Charley, I can't think of Charley's name, but, anyhow, this fellow was a very good friend. And I worked a season there. That was when I worked with the two Ethels and there was a fellow named Snow Fisher, he was a great strutter, and a girl named Izzy Ringgold was a great dancer, come from a dancing family.
Okay, now, the two Ethels were Ethel Waters and Ethel White.
Ethel Williams and Ethel Waters. Right.
They were the two Ethels. And at that time they were good friends and they were even -- and they had a like a sister team, and they even had their clothes alike, you know?
Yeah. And Ethel Waters -- er, Williams was the dancer and Ethel Williams, I mean Ethel Waters, was the singer.
Ethel Waters was never a great singer. But she was a -- more of an entertainer.
No, Ethel Waters was a singer, but not much of a singer. And Ethel Williams was a good, very good dancer. Eccentric dancer, like.
But you don't think Ethel Waters was much of a singer.
And she had never been. And she ain't much of a singer. But she's been an entertainer with a very pleasing voice, but she wasn't any singer.

The way I know as singing, that somebody can sing -- she may have been what we call a crooner. At that time there wasn't no name for it. There wasn't no name, 'crooner', but she'd never been a great singer.
